I have been farming these 10.1 mu for most of my life. With my wife — just the two of us in the household — I cannot spread myself too thin, so I stick to what I know: wheat-maize rotation on the better 7 mu, and 3.1 mu of cotton on the sandier piece that never did well for grain. My well gives me control, which matters more each year as the spring rains get less reliable.

For **winter wheat** on 7 mu: I sow an improved semi-dwarf variety — Jimai or Shimai line, same as most neighbors around Quzhou use now. I put down diammonium phosphate and potassium chloride as base before sowing, then topdress urea at jointing in March. That comes out to about 16 kg N, 8 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O per mu. I irrigate 3 times — the winter water in December, jointing in late March, and grain-filling in early May. Two sprays: one for aphids and powdery mildew at heading, one combined with foliar KH₂PO₄ for grain filling. I plough once every two-three years, rotary-till the other years; this year is rotary. I expect 480 kg per mu — my land is decent but not the best in the village.

For **summer maize** on the same 7 mu after wheat harvest: no-till direct seeding into the stubble the day after combining, that is how everyone does it now to save time. Zhengdan 958 or Denghai hybrid. Fertilizer goes in at sowing and a topdressing at large-flare stage — 18 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O per mu. One irrigation if July is dry, sometimes two. One spray for corn borer at whorl stage, maybe a second for armyworm if I see them. I look for 600 kg per mu.

For **cotton** on 3.1 mu: Bt hybrid seed, I have used transgenic cotton for over twenty years, no going back. Cotton eats a lot of potassium, so I put more K here — 14 kg N, 7 kg P₂O₅, 9 kg K₂O per mu, split across basal, squaring, and flowering. Plough before sowing to loosen the soil. Irrigate twice — at squaring and flowering. Cotton needs the most spraying of anything I grow — six sprays for aphids, mirids, bollworm escapes from Bt, and spider mites in August. I target 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.
